'''Joel C. Kleinman''' (1946 – May 2, 1991) was an American health statistician and epidemiologist specializing on the causes of infant mortality. He was director of analysis at the [[National Center for Health Statistics]].

==Life==
Kleinman was born in 1946 in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York City|New York]] to Rose and George Kleinman.<ref name=":25">{{Cite news |date=1991-05-08 |title=Joel C. Kleinman, 44, A Health Statistician |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1991/05/08/obituaries/joel-c-kleinman-44-a-health-statistician.html |access-date=2023-06-04 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Kiely |first=John |date=October 1991 |title=Obituary |journal=Paediatric and Perinatal Epidemiology |language=en |volume=5 |issue=4 |pages=465–468 |doi=10.1111/j.1365-3016.1991.tb00733.x|pmid=1754504 }}</ref> He was raised in [[the Bronx]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1967, he earned a bachelor's degree from [[City College of New York]].<ref name=":25" /><ref name=":0" /> He completed a master's degree and Ph.D. in statistics (1971) from [[Harvard University]].<ref name=":25" /> He worked there as an assistant professor of biostatistics from 1971 to 1975.<ref name=":25" /><ref name=":0" /> In 1975, Kleinman joined the [[National Center for Health Statistics]] as a visiting service fellow.<ref name=":25" /><ref name=":0" /> He became its director of analysis in 1980.<ref name=":0" /> In 1982, Kleinman won the [[Mortimer Spiegelman Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Awards |url=https://www.apha.org/apha-communities/member-sections/applied-public-health-statistics/who-we-are/awards |access-date=2023-06-04 |website=www.apha.org}}</ref> In 1990, he was elected a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=American Statistical Association |url=https://www.amstat.org/ |access-date=2023-06-04 |website=American Statistical Association}}</ref> A health statistician and epidemiologist, he specialized on the causes of infant mortality.<ref name=":25" /><ref name=":0" />

Kleinman was married to cell biologist [[Hynda Kleinman]].<ref name=":25" /> They had two daughters.<ref name=":25" /> He died of diabetes complications on May 2, 1991, during a business trip in [[Berkeley Springs, West Virginia]].<ref name=":25" />
